scope: Proposition 5.1 (The root clocks) of the manuscript “Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation” (preprints/Scalar-Potentials-and-Slow-Clocks-for-Forced-Fluid-Computation-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 82005335f0aac60f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.1, set g(t) = (1 + t)q − 1, where q = 1/3 or q = 1/4, and put β = 1 − q. All mixed derivatives of the velocity and force in (5) are bounded, and for every fixed j, α, ∥∂j t Dα x u(t)∥∞ + ∥∂j t Dα x f(t)∥∞ ≤ Cj,α(1 + t)−β . In particular each is square-integrable in time in spatial supremum norm. The cube-root exponent is 2/3 and the fourth-root exponent is 3/4.
